title: Diljit Dosanjh, AR Rahman and Imtiaz Ali Are About to Break Your Heart. Main Vaapas Aaunga Arrives Friday.
excerpt: A Partition love story spanning 80 years, with a soundtrack that made Toronto weep and a first review that calls it unforgettable. Advance bookings are already open in North America.
body:
The last time Imtiaz Ali and Diljit Dosanjh made a film together, they turned a Chamkila biopic into one of the most devastating love stories of the streaming era. Now they're back. And this time, they've brought A.R. Rahman, Naseeruddin Shah, Vedang Raina, and Sharvari along for the ride.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PRUTWluKRW8

Main Vaapas Aaunga — which translates to "I Will Return" — arrives in cinemas this Friday, June 12. It is a Partition love story. It spans 80 years. It runs 167 minutes. And if the early reactions are any indication, you should bring tissues.

A Love Story Written in Two Timelines

The film unfolds across two eras. In the first, set in an undivided India on the cusp of 1947, a mild-mannered aspiring poet named Keenu (Vedang Raina) falls for Jiya (Sharvari), a young woman who isn't afraid of taking the lead. Their romance is sun-drenched and tender — Sharvari riding a bicycle through open fields while Raina runs behind her in a sardar's costume, the kind of image that lingers.

In the second timeline, Keenu is now an ageing man (Naseeruddin Shah), writing his story from a hospital bed, desperate to return to the hometown he lost to Partition — now across the border in Pakistan. His grandson, played by Diljit Dosanjh, carries the weight of that longing into the present.

"In Imtiaz Ali's world, love is never just a feeling. It is a journey that lingers in stolen glances, unfinished conversations, and memories that refuse to fade away." — The makers

Imtiaz Ali co-wrote the screenplay with Nayanika Mahtani, and the film was shot entirely in Punjab between August and December 2025, with cinematography by Sylvester Fonseca and editing by Aarti Bajaj — both long-time Imtiaz collaborators.

Rahman's Score Is Already Drawing Tears

The music has been quietly building anticipation for months. A.R. Rahman composed the score, with lyrics by the indispensable Irshad Kamil — the same duo behind Rockstar, Tamasha, and Highway. Three singles have dropped so far: "Kya Kamaal Hai" (sung by Diljit himself), the haunting "Maskara" (Nilanjana Ghosh and Vedang Raina), and "Vo Nahin."

And then there was the Attari border concert. On June 7, Rahman performed at the India-Pakistan border — the first artist ever to do so — in a tribute to BSF soldiers titled Jai Ho: A Tribute to the Bravehearts. Vedang Raina sang live. Mohit Chauhan performed "Ishq Mastana." The evening closed with "Maa Tujhe Salaam."

"This event is around Main Vaapas Aaunga, a film that originates from the making of the border during the Partition of 1947. Not only homes and lives were lost, but hearts were broken as well. We bring a message of love because, ultimately, only love sustains us." — Imtiaz Ali

Toronto Saw It First — And Lost Its Mind

Diljit, currently tearing through North America on his AURA Tour 2026, screened the trailer at a packed Toronto stadium. The reaction? Thunderous. Fans have flooded social media with clips, and advance bookings are already open across the US and Canada — a week ahead of India — thanks to overwhelming international demand.

The Diaspora Angle

For NRIs, Main Vaapas Aaunga hits different. The story of a man trying to return to a home that no longer exists in the same country is not just historical drama — it's living memory for millions of families across the diaspora. The Partition displaced 15 million people, and many never went back. This film resonates deeply, echoing the experiences of those who navigate the complexities of identity, belonging, and family ties across borders. It serves as a poignant reminder of the emotional scars that many Indian families carry, making it a must-watch for the diaspora.

Ektaa Kapoor, who saw an early screening, called it "a film that stayed with me even after it ended." She praised Diljit's "restrained" performance, called Vedang Raina the film's "surprise package," and described Rahman's music as "pure magic."

Reactions from the diaspora have been overwhelmingly positive, with many expressing how the film's themes of love and loss resonate with their own family histories. Social media is abuzz with anticipation, as audiences eagerly await the film's release, hoping to connect with their roots through its narrative.

The supporting cast includes Rajat Kapoor, Manish Chaudhary, Anjana Sukhani, Danish Pandor, and Banita Sandhu. Produced by Applause Entertainment, Birla Studios, and Window Seat Films, Main Vaapas Aaunga is distributed worldwide by Birla Studios.

This Friday. Cinemas everywhere. Bring someone you love — and something to cry into.
